subject: Business
title: The Semiconductor Supply Chain
description: One-minute skill: The Semiconductor Supply Chain.

hook.text: A single advanced chip requires 1,000+ process steps across 70+ border crossings before reaching your phone.

buildup.text: The semiconductor supply chain is the most complex on Earth: design in the US, fabrication in Taiwan, packaging in Malaysia.

discovery.text: TSMC in Taiwan produces over 90% of the world's most advanced chips. One earthquake could cripple global tech.

twist.text: The 2021 chip shortage idled $210 billion in auto production. A $1 chip held up $40,000 cars.

climax.text: The US CHIPS Act is investing $52 billion to build domestic chip fabs, reducing dependence on Taiwan.

punchline.text: The most important supply chain in the world runs through a single island.

quiz.question: What percentage of the world's most advanced chips does TSMC produce?

details.summary: The semiconductor supply chain is one of the most complex and geographically concentrated in the world. Designing chips in the US, fabricating them primarily in Taiwan and South Korea, and assembling them in Southeast Asia creates dependencies that have drawn intense geopolitical attention.
details.whyItMatters: Semiconductors power every modern electronic device. The 2020-2023 chip shortage halted auto production and raised consumer prices, demonstrating how this single supply chain can disrupt entire economies and national security interests.
takeaways: Chip design, fabrication, and assembly are spread across different continents
Taiwan produces over 60 percent of the world's semiconductors
The global chip shortage cost the auto industry tens of billions in lost revenue

faq.question: Why is the semiconductor supply chain so geographically concentrated?
faq.answer: Fabrication requires tens of billions in investment per facility and decades of expertise. TSMC and Samsung achieved scale advantages that make new entry extremely difficult. ASML in the Netherlands is the sole producer of extreme UV lithography machines essential for advanced chips.

faq.question: What are governments doing to address semiconductor supply chain risks?
faq.answer: The US CHIPS Act provides over 50 billion dollars for domestic fabrication. The EU Chips Act targets similar investment. Japan, South Korea, and India have launched incentive programs. These aim to diversify production geographically but building capacity takes years.
